Morley-Minto Reforms *In 1905, Lord Curzon was replaced by Lord Minto as Viceroy of India and John Morley was secretary of India then. Morley-Minto Reforms are related to the reforms initiated by these two. These constitutional reforms were passed by British Government and ofﬁ cially they were called Indian Council Act, 1909. It is generally known as Morley-Minto Reforms. The biggest blunder of this reform was the separate electorate given to Muslim community under the Communal representation system. According to this system, the Muslim candidates into the council were not elected by general Electoral but were elected by the Muslim voters only. This system accepted Muslims as a separate community in India. This created many fundamental issues in India. The unity of India was attacked and demolished in just a stroke. Gandhiji said - “Morley Minto reform has destroyed us completely". 1. Morley-Minto Reform Bill was passed in : (a) 1905 (b) 1909 (c) 1911 (d) 1920 U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1994 Ans. (b) In 1905, Lord Minto was appointed as Viceroy of India in place of Lord Curzon and John Morley was appointed as Secretary of India. The reforms introduced by them are known as Morley-Minto Reforms. The Indian Councils Act, 1909, commonly known as the Morley-Minto Reforms was an Act of the Parliament of the United Kingdom that brought about a limited increase in the involvement of Indians in the governance of British India. The major dispute regarding this bill was separate electorate for Muslim in India. 2. Which of the following Act provided for communal representation in British India? Lucknow Session of Congress (The Lucknow Pact) *In December 1916, both Indian National Congress and Muslim League held their sessions at Lucknow. *Both parties passed separate resolutions on demands of constitutional reforms and agreed on a pact to work together in the political ﬁ eld on a common programme. This is known as Lucknow Pact or Congress-League Programme. *Ambika Charan Mazumdar was president of Congress in this session. As a result, they together released 19 bulletins to give a positive direction to the contemporary political scenario. *Lucknow session was very signiﬁ cant due to two reasons, ﬁ rst, the Extremists who were expelled from Congress nine years ago (in 1907) were again merged to Congress and, secondly there was a pact between Congress and League. Annie Besant and Tilak played a signiﬁ cant role in the return of Extremists to Congress on the other hand, the efforts of Jinnah and Tilak were responsible for Congress-League Pact. The period from 1916 to 1922 was the time of consensus between Congress and League. Lucknow Pact was just a temporary arrangement. Muslim League, besides this pact had its own identity and it advocated for the interests of Muslims where ever possible. Both League and Congress were together till 1922.
